Semipositivity of θ makes θ+ηh strictly positive for every η>0, so zero potentials establish exactly the requested nefness. Since a is nonconstant, da∧w is nonzero somewhere, proving nonclosedness.

The radial normalization and determinant calculations check out with the stipulated dd^c convention and ordinary wedge powers. The Fubini–Study radial density is m s^(m−1)(1+s)^(−m−1) ds, becoming m x^(m−1) dx. Consequently ∫_B ω^m/a=mt/(m−1)=1. For a radial potential F, the Hessian determinant is (q/s)^(m−1)dq/ds, where q=sF′. Dividing by the Fubini–Study determinant gives q^(m−1)(dq/dx)/x^(m−1). Unverified independent proof draft. Artifacts are retained in /workspace/research/native-workers/codex-CIMYHz: input.json, proof.txt, verify_radial.py, checks.txt, execution.txt, package_notes.py and notes.json. Rerun the diagnostics with `python verify_radial.py > checks.txt`; package the notes with `python package_notes.py`. No external mathematical source or computational result is an indispensable premise.

Fix any integer m≥2, n=m+1 and t=(m−1)/m. Throughout, dd^c=i∂bar∂/(2π). On B=P^m set x=Σ_{j=1}^m|Z_j|²/Σ_{j=0}^m|Z_j|² and a=x/t. The quotient is globally smooth: every projective chart has a strictly positive denominator. It takes values in [0,1], vanishes exactly at p=[1:0:…:0], and is nonconstant. These establish the corresponding claims about a.

On U0={Z0≠0}, write z_j=Z_j/Z0, s=Σ|z_j|² and x=s/(1+s). Normalized Fubini–Study is ω=dd^c log(1+s). For a radial potential R(s), put q(x)=sR′(s). Its Hessian has tangential eigenvalue q/s, with multiplicity m−1, and radial eigenvalue dq/ds=(1−x)²q′(x). The corresponding eigenvalues of ω are 1−x and (1−x)². Consequently, for s>0,

(dd^cR)^m/ω^m=(q/x)^(m−1)q′(x).                         (1)

If R=log(1+s)+ψ(x), direct differentiation gives

q=x+x(1−x)ψ′(x),   ψ′(x)=(q−x)/[x(1−x)].              (2)

Both forms use the specified dd^c, so their determinant ratio has no additional normalization factor.

The same normalization gives the polar formula

∫_B F(x)ω^m=m∫_0^1 F(y)y^(m−1)dy.                     (3)

Indeed, on C^m, ω^m=m!π^(−m)(1+s)^(−m−1)dV. Polar integration yields density m s^(m−1)(1+s)^(−m−1)ds, and substitution x=s/(1+s) yields (3). The omitted projective hyperplane has smooth volume zero. The formula applies to nonnegative measurable functions, including the integrands below.

For every ε>0 define

bε(x)=x/t+ε,
Hε=m∫_0^1 y^(m−1)/bε(y)dy,
Qε(x)=(m/Hε)∫_0^x y^(m−1)/bε(y)dy,
qε(x)=Qε(x)^(1/m) for x>0, with qε(0)=0,
ψε(x)=∫_0^x [qε(y)−y]/[y(1−y)]dy.                    (4)

The endpoint extensions in this expression are proved next. Hε is finite and positive, and qε(1)=1. Differentiation on 0<x≤1 gives

qε′=x^(m−1)/[Hε bε qε^(m−1)]>0,
(qε/x)^(m−1)qε′=1/[Hε bε].                            (5)

At zero, substitution y=xu gives Qε(x)=x^m kε(x), where

kε(x)=(m/Hε)∫_0^1 u^(m−1)/(xu/t+ε)du.

This function is smooth and strictly positive on a neighborhood of [0,1]. Thus qε=x kε^(1/m) extends smoothly across zero, and

qε′(0)=[1/(Hεε)]^(1/m)>0.

Equation (2) becomes ψε′=[kε^(1/m)−1]/(1−x), which is smooth at zero. At one, kε(1)=1, so the numerator vanishes and division by 1−x is removable. Hence ψε extends smoothly to a neighborhood of [0,1], with

ψε′(1)=1−qε′(1),   qε′(1)=1/[Hε(1/t+ε)]>0.            (6)

Therefore ψε(x) is a globally smooth function on B. Let Aε=ω+dd^cψε(x). Equations (1) and (5) give strict positivity on U0 minus p and the determinant identity Aε^m/ω^m=1/[Hεbε]. At p, the Hessian extends as Aε(p)=qε′(0)ω(p), so it is strictly positive and has determinant ratio 1/(Hεε).

Every infinity chart can also be checked explicitly. On U_j={Z_j≠0}, j≥1, write ζ_k=Z_k/Z_j for k≠j, S=1+Σ_{k≠j}|ζ_k|², and S0=1+Σ_{k≠j,0}|ζ_k|². Here ω=dd^c log S and x=1−|ζ0|²/S. On ζ0=0, for any smooth ψ near 1, dd^cψ(x) has zero tangential and mixed blocks and normal coefficient −ψ′(1)/S0, with the common dd^c factor understood. The normal coefficient of ω is 1/S0. Thus Aε has its positive Fubini–Study tangential block and normal coefficient qε′(1)/S0. Its determinant ratio there is qε′(1)=1/[Hεbε(1)]. These charts cover the entire hyperplane x=1. Consequently Aε is globally smooth, closed and strictly positive, and its determinant identity holds everywhere.

We now prove genuine admissibility of the proposed limiting potential at p by global approximation. Put c=tε and J_c(x)=∫_0^x y^(m−1)/(y+c)dy. Then qε(x)^m=J_c(x)/J_c(1). For 0<x≤1, the two equivalent substitutions

J_c(x)=x^m∫_0^1 u^(m−1)/(xu+c)du
       =x^(m−1)∫_0^1 u^(m−1)/(u+c/x)du

show, respectively, that J_c(x)/J_c(1)≥x^m and ≤x^(m−1). Hence

x≤qε(x)≤x^t.                                         (7)

As ε↓0, convergence under the integral gives

Hε→mt∫_0^1 y^(m−2)dy=1,
Qε(x)→x^(m−1),   qε(x)→x^t                           (8)

for 0<x≤1. The dominating density for Hε is mt y^(m−2), integrable also when m=2.

Define exactly the potential specified in the target:

φ(x)=∫_0^x (y^t−y)/[y(1−y)]dy.

Its derivative is φ′(x)=[x^(t−1)−1]/(1−x). This is O(x^(t−1)) near zero, hence integrable because t>0. At one it has a smooth extension with value 1−t. Therefore φ is bounded continuous on [0,1], φ(0)=0, and φ is smooth on (0,1], including a smooth extension across one.

Equations (7)–(8) imply 0≤ψε′≤φ′ on (0,1) and ψε′→φ′ pointwise. Dominated convergence therefore gives

sup_[0,1]|ψε−φ|≤∫_0^1|ψε′−φ′|dx→0.                   (9)

This is uniform convergence of globally smooth genuine ω-psh functions on compact B. In every chart, adding a smooth local potential ρ for ω gives psh functions ρ+ψε converging uniformly to the continuous function ρ+φ. The permitted uniform-limit property makes ρ+φ psh with its canonical representative, including at p. This proves global genuine admissibility at p, without assuming a punctured-point extension theorem or a restriction. The value φ(p)=0 is its continuous canonical value. Thus A=ω+dd^cφ is globally positive and closed as a current, also the distributional limit of Aε.

Away from p, q=x^t in (1), so

A^m/ω^m=(x^t/x)^(m−1)t x^(t−1)=t/x=1/a.              (10)

Both radial eigenvalues are positive. On each infinity chart the preceding block calculation applies with φ′(1)=1−t: the normal relative eigenvalue is t>0, and tangential relative eigenvalues are 1. The determinant ratio is therefore t, agreeing with (10) at x=1. This establishes smooth strict positivity everywhere off p, including projective infinity.

Finally, the polar formula proves

∫_B ω^m/a=mt∫_0^1 y^(m−2)dy=1.                       (11)

The measure-zero singular point does not alter this ordinary integral and no canonical function value is modified.

Unverified independent proof draft, using the radial construction established in n1. Artifacts are retained in /workspace/research/native-workers/codex-CIMYHz: proof.txt, verify_radial.py, checks.txt, execution.txt, package_notes.py, notes.json and input.json. Let X=B×P1, m≥2 and n=m+1. All forms from either factor are implicitly pulled back. Let w be normalized Fubini–Study on P1, h=ω+w and μ=ω^m∧w. This is a smooth strictly positive probability volume. Use n1’s globally smooth positive closed Aε=ω+dd^cψε, its determinant Aε^m/ω^m=1/[Hε(a+ε)], and Hε=m∫_0^1 y^(m−1)/(y/t+ε)dy.

Fix arbitrary constants c>0 and ε>0 and put b=a+ε,

β=cω+bw,
T=cAε+bw=β+dd^c(cψε),
K=nc^m/Hε.

Both β and T are smooth strictly positive forms. Ordinary wedge algebra, using w²=0 and Aε pulled back from the m-dimensional base, gives

T^n=nc^m b Aε^m∧w=Kμ.                                (1)

This is an identity of smooth differential forms; it uses no nonclosed product mass theorem.

Let γ be any smooth positive Gauduchon metric on X, with dd^cγ^m=0. Stokes gives

∫_X β∧γ^m=∫_X T∧γ^m.

At every point, matrix AM–GM gives

T∧γ^m=(tr_γT/n)γ^n
      ≥(T^n/γ^n)^(1/n)γ^n
      =K^(1/n)(μ/γ^n)^(1/n)γ^n.

Integration proves that the defining quotient is at least K^(1/n) for every metric in the full Gauduchon family. No selected test family is substituted for that infimum.

An actual attaining metric is

γε,c=b^(−1/m)(cAε+bw).                                (2)

The coefficient b is globally smooth and bounded below by ε, and Aε is globally smooth strictly positive by n1’s endpoint and chart checks. Thus (2) is a globally smooth positive Hermitian metric. Its m-th power is

γε,c^m=b^(−1)c^mAε^m+mc^(m−1)Aε^(m−1)∧w.             (3)

The first summand is pulled back from a top-degree form on B. It is d-closed even though its coefficient varies. The second is d-closed because Aε and w are closed. Consequently dγε,c^m=0, hence dd^cγε,c^m=0. This proves that (2) is an admissible Gauduchon metric, indeed a balanced metric.

It is conformal to T, so all matrix eigenvalues in AM–GM agree and equality holds pointwise. Every normalization can also be checked directly. Equations (1)–(2) give

γε,c^n=Kb^(−n/m)μ.

Therefore

Dμ(γε,c)=∫_X (μ/γε,c^n)^(1/n)γε,c^n
         =K^(m/n)∫_X μ/b
         =K^(m/n)Hε.

The last equality is n1’s polar formula and ∫_P1w=1. Stokes and conformality give

∫_X β∧γε,c^m=∫_X T∧γε,c^m
             =K∫_X μ/b=KHε=nc^m.

Thus this metric’s quotient is K^(1/n), exactly the universal lower bound. We have proved

λμ(cω+(a+ε)w)=(nc^m/Hε)^(1/n),
Vμ(cω+(a+ε)w)=nc^m/Hε                                (4)

against the entire defining family.

For c=1, β=θε=ω+(a+ε)w is smooth strictly positive and (4) gives Vμ(θε)=n/Hε. The metrics γε,1 are actual smooth global Gauduchon minimizers for every ε>0. The limit Hε→1 and all radial endpoint smoothness are proved in n1, without invoking a global PDE.

For an optional explicit evaluation, put d=tε>0. Polynomial division in the defining integral gives

Hε=mt[Σ_{j=0}^{m−2}(−d)^j/(m−1−j)
       +(−d)^(m−1)log((1+d)/d)].                       (5)

This expression is a reformulation of the strictly positive integral. Positivity and convergence are justified by that integral, avoiding cancellation arguments in the finite sum. In particular the m=2 logarithmic term causes no difficulty: the dominating density mt y^(m−2) is integrable for every m≥2.

Ancillary retained evidence: symbolic conformal-exponent checks passed, and (5) was checked symbolically for m=2,…,12. At 65 decimal digits, the finite samples m=2,3,4,7 and ε=1,0.1,0.001 gave agreement between quadrature and (5), with maximum sampled residual 7.1216758×10^(−66). For m=2 and ε=0.1, Hε=0.847773878113829, K=3.53867944914103, numerator=3 and D=1.96867569726271; the cube of the quotient equals K to the displayed precision. These computations are diagnostics; the universal equality and existence statements follow from the written construction and inequalities.

Artifacts are in /workspace/research/native-workers/codex-CIMYHz: input.json, proof.txt, verify_radial.py, checks.txt, execution.txt, package_notes.py and notes.json. Fix any m≥2, n=m+1 and t=(m−1)/m. On X=P^m×P1 use the forms, coefficient a=x/t, probability volume μ=ω^m∧w and Hermitian form h=ω+w from n1–n2. Define θ=ω+aw.

This background is globally smooth semipositive. For every η>0,

θ+ηh=(1+η)ω+(a+η)w

is smooth strictly positive. Potential zero therefore proves nefness in exactly the assignment’s sense. It is genuinely nonclosed: dθ=da∧w. Since a is nonconstant, da is nonzero somewhere; evaluation on a suitable base vector and a vertical pair with w positive shows da∧w is nonzero.

Pull back n1’s φ to X. It is bounded continuous and genuinely global quasi-psh: locally the pullback of the base psh function ρ+φ is psh, and subtracting the smooth pullback of ρ gives φ. Its canonical value along E={p}×P1 is zero. Its θ-current is

T=θ+dd^cφ=A+aw.

By n1, A is globally positive, and a≥0, so T is positive globally. On X minus E, A is smooth strictly positive and a>0. Hence T is smooth strictly positive there. On that complement, ordinary wedge algebra and A^m/ω^m=1/a give

T^n=naA^m∧w=nμ.                                      (1)

No global top product of this singular nonclosed current is assumed or asserted.

Now let γ be any smooth positive Gauduchon metric, with dd^cγ^m=0. Because φ is bounded, distributional Stokes applies and gives

∫_X θ∧γ^m=∫_X T∧γ^m.

The right side is the total mass of a positive finite measure obtained by wedging the positive (1,1) current with a smooth positive form. On X minus E it is the ordinary smooth form. Equation (1) and matrix AM–GM there give

T∧γ^m≥n^(1/n)(μ/γ^n)^(1/n)γ^n.

Fix any integer m≥2, n=m+1 and t=(m−1)/m. Throughout, dd^c=i∂bar∂/(2π). On B=P^m set x=Σ_{j=1}^m|Z_j|²/Σ_{j=0}^m|Z_j|² and a=x/t. The quotient is globally smooth: every projective chart has a strictly positive denominator. It takes values in [0,1], vanishes exactly at p=[1:0:…:0], and is nonconstant. These establish the corresponding claims about a.

On U0={Z0≠0}, write z_j=Z_j/Z0, s=Σ|z_j|² and x=s/(1+s). Normalized Fubini–Study is ω=dd^c log(1+s). For a radial potential R(s), put q(x)=sR′(s). Its Hessian has tangential eigenvalue q/s, with multiplicity m−1, and radial eigenvalue dq/ds=(1−x)²q′(x). The corresponding eigenvalues of ω are 1−x and (1−x)². Consequently, for s>0,

(dd^cR)^m/ω^m=(q/x)^(m−1)q′(x).                         (1)

If R=log(1+s)+ψ(x), direct differentiation gives

q=x+x(1−x)ψ′(x),   ψ′(x)=(q−x)/[x(1−x)].              (2)

Both forms use the specified dd^c, so their determinant ratio has no additional normalization factor.

The same normalization gives the polar formula

∫_B F(x)ω^m=m∫_0^1 F(y)y^(m−1)dy.                     (3)

Indeed, on C^m, ω^m=m!π^(−m)(1+s)^(−m−1)dV. Polar integration yields density m s^(m−1)(1+s)^(−m−1)ds, and substitution x=s/(1+s) yields (3). The omitted projective hyperplane has smooth volume zero. The formula applies to nonnegative measurable functions, including the integrands below.

For every ε>0 define

bε(x)=x/t+ε,
Hε=m∫_0^1 y^(m−1)/bε(y)dy,
Qε(x)=(m/Hε)∫_0^x y^(m−1)/bε(y)dy,
qε(x)=Qε(x)^(1/m) for x>0, with qε(0)=0,
ψε(x)=∫_0^x [qε(y)−y]/[y(1−y)]dy.                    (4)

The endpoint extensions in this expression are proved next. Hε is finite and positive, and qε(1)=1. Differentiation on 0<x≤1 gives

qε′=x^(m−1)/[Hε bε qε^(m−1)]>0,
(qε/x)^(m−1)qε′=1/[Hε bε].                            (5)

At zero, substitution y=xu gives Qε(x)=x^m kε(x), where

kε(x)=(m/Hε)∫_0^1 u^(m−1)/(xu/t+ε)du.

This function is smooth and strictly positive on a neighborhood of [0,1]. Thus qε=x kε^(1/m) extends smoothly across zero, and

qε′(0)=[1/(Hεε)]^(1/m)>0.

Equation (2) becomes ψε′=[kε^(1/m)−1]/(1−x), which is smooth at zero. At one, kε(1)=1, so the numerator vanishes and division by 1−x is removable. Hence ψε extends smoothly to a neighborhood of [0,1], with

ψε′(1)=1−qε′(1),   qε′(1)=1/[Hε(1/t+ε)]>0.            (6)

Therefore ψε(x) is a globally smooth function on B. Let Aε=ω+dd^cψε(x). Equations (1) and (5) give strict positivity on U0 minus p and the determinant identity Aε^m/ω^m=1/[Hεbε]. At p, the Hessian extends as Aε(p)=qε′(0)ω(p), so it is strictly positive and has determinant ratio 1/(Hεε).

Every infinity chart can also be checked explicitly. On U_j={Z_j≠0}, j≥1, write ζ_k=Z_k/Z_j for k≠j, S=1+Σ_{k≠j}|ζ_k|², and S0=1+Σ_{k≠j,0}|ζ_k|². Here ω=dd^c log S and x=1−|ζ0|²/S. On ζ0=0, for any smooth ψ near 1, dd^cψ(x) has zero tangential and mixed blocks and normal coefficient −ψ′(1)/S0, with the common dd^c factor understood. The normal coefficient of ω is 1/S0. Thus Aε has its positive Fubini–Study tangential block and normal coefficient qε′(1)/S0. Its determinant ratio there is qε′(1)=1/[Hεbε(1)]. These charts cover the entire hyperplane x=1. Consequently Aε is globally smooth, closed and strictly positive, and its determinant identity holds everywhere.

We now prove genuine admissibility of the proposed limiting potential at p by global approximation. Put c=tε and J_c(x)=∫_0^x y^(m−1)/(y+c)dy. Then qε(x)^m=J_c(x)/J_c(1). For 0<x≤1, the two equivalent substitutions

J_c(x)=x^m∫_0^1 u^(m−1)/(xu+c)du
       =x^(m−1)∫_0^1 u^(m−1)/(u+c/x)du

show, respectively, that J_c(x)/J_c(1)≥x^m and ≤x^(m−1). Hence

x≤qε(x)≤x^t.                                         (7)

As ε↓0, convergence under the integral gives

Hε→mt∫_0^1 y^(m−2)dy=1,
Qε(x)→x^(m−1),   qε(x)→x^t                           (8)

for 0<x≤1. The dominating density for Hε is mt y^(m−2), integrable also when m=2.

Define exactly the potential specified in the target:

φ(x)=∫_0^x (y^t−y)/[y(1−y)]dy.

Its derivative is φ′(x)=[x^(t−1)−1]/(1−x). This is O(x^(t−1)) near zero, hence integrable because t>0. At one it has a smooth extension with value 1−t. Therefore φ is bounded continuous on [0,1], φ(0)=0, and φ is smooth on (0,1], including a smooth extension across one.

Equations (7)–(8) imply 0≤ψε′≤φ′ on (0,1) and ψε′→φ′ pointwise. Dominated convergence therefore gives

sup_[0,1]|ψε−φ|≤∫_0^1|ψε′−φ′|dx→0.                   (9)

This is uniform convergence of globally smooth genuine ω-psh functions on compact B. In every chart, adding a smooth local potential ρ for ω gives psh functions ρ+ψε converging uniformly to the continuous function ρ+φ. The permitted uniform-limit property makes ρ+φ psh with its canonical representative, including at p. This proves global genuine admissibility at p, without assuming a punctured-point extension theorem or a restriction. The value φ(p)=0 is its continuous canonical value. Thus A=ω+dd^cφ is globally positive and closed as a current, also the distributional limit of Aε.

Away from p, q=x^t in (1), so

A^m/ω^m=(x^t/x)^(m−1)t x^(t−1)=t/x=1/a.              (10)

Both radial eigenvalues are positive. On each infinity chart the preceding block calculation applies with φ′(1)=1−t: the normal relative eigenvalue is t>0, and tangential relative eigenvalues are 1. The determinant ratio is therefore t, agreeing with (10) at x=1. This establishes smooth strict positivity everywhere off p, including projective infinity.

Finally, the polar formula proves

∫_B ω^m/a=mt∫_0^1 y^(m−2)dy=1.                       (11)

The measure-zero singular point does not alter this ordinary integral and no canonical function value is modified.

Unverified independent proof draft, using n1 and n2. Artifacts are in /workspace/research/native-workers/codex-CIMYHz: input.json, proof.txt, verify_radial.py, checks.txt, execution.txt, package_notes.py and notes.json. Fix any m≥2, n=m+1 and t=(m−1)/m. On X=P^m×P1 use the forms, coefficient a=x/t, probability volume μ=ω^m∧w and Hermitian form h=ω+w from n1–n2. Define θ=ω+aw.

This background is globally smooth semipositive. For every η>0,

θ+ηh=(1+η)ω+(a+η)w

is smooth strictly positive. Potential zero therefore proves nefness in exactly the assignment’s sense. It is genuinely nonclosed: dθ=da∧w. Since a is nonconstant, da is nonzero somewhere; evaluation on a suitable base vector and a vertical pair with w positive shows da∧w is nonzero.

Pull back n1’s φ to X. It is bounded continuous and genuinely global quasi-psh: locally the pullback of the base psh function ρ+φ is psh, and subtracting the smooth pullback of ρ gives φ. Its canonical value along E={p}×P1 is zero. Its θ-current is

T=θ+dd^cφ=A+aw.

By n1, A is globally positive, and a≥0, so T is positive globally. On X minus E, A is smooth strictly positive and a>0. Hence T is smooth strictly positive there. On that complement, ordinary wedge algebra and A^m/ω^m=1/a give

T^n=naA^m∧w=nμ.                                      (1)

No global top product of this singular nonclosed current is assumed or asserted.

Now let γ be any smooth positive Gauduchon metric, with dd^cγ^m=0. Because φ is bounded, distributional Stokes applies and gives

∫_X θ∧γ^m=∫_X T∧γ^m.

The right side is the total mass of a positive finite measure obtained by wedging the positive (1,1) current with a smooth positive form. On X minus E it is the ordinary smooth form. Equation (1) and matrix AM–GM there give

T∧γ^m≥n^(1/n)(μ/γ^n)^(1/n)γ^n.

Discarding any nonnegative measure mass on E preserves this inequality after integration. E has zero smooth volume, so the right-hand integral over its complement is the entire Dμ(γ). Therefore

∫_X θ∧γ^m/Dμ(γ)≥n^(1/n)                              (2)

for every smooth positive Gauduchon metric in the defining infimum.

For the reverse bound, use n2’s actual smooth minimizers γε for θε=ω+(a+ε)w. Since θ≤θε and γε^m is positive,

λμ(θ)≤∫_X θ∧γε^m/Dμ(γε)
      ≤∫_X θε∧γε^m/Dμ(γε)
      =(n/Hε)^(1/n).

By n1, Hε→1 as ε↓0. Together with (2), this proves

λμ(θ)=n^(1/n),   Vμ(θ)=n.                             (3)

Indeed the displayed quotients for γε are squeezed to n^(1/n), so these are actual smooth minimizing tests in the limiting sense. No smooth attaining test for θ itself is claimed.

The original boundary definition uses θ+ηh, rather than just θε. Apply n2’s more general formula with c=1+η and ε=η. It gives exactly

Vμ(θ+ηh)=n(1+η)^m/Hη,
λμ(θ+ηh)=[n(1+η)^m/Hη]^(1/n).                         (4)

As η↓0, the limits are n and n^(1/n). For each fixed metric, the numerator decreases as η decreases, so its infimum also decreases. Thus (4) computes the prescribed decreasing Hermitian regularization and proves that it agrees with the direct nonnegative full infimum (3). Neither the density nor the defining metric family was replaced.

Nonbigness excludes all genuine global quasi-psh potentials by a distributional test. Suppose a genuine global quasi-psh v and δ>0 satisfied

S=θ+dd^cv−δh≥0.

Such a potential is locally integrable wherever this global current is defined. Let η_B be any smooth nonnegative top-degree (m,m) form on B, and let π:X→B be projection. Its pullback is a smooth semipositive (n−1,n−1) form. Positivity gives

0≤∫_X S∧π*η_B.

If strict positivity is required for test-form terminology, first use π*η_B+τh^m and let τ↓0. Because η_B is top-degree on the base, dd^cη_B=0. Distributional Stokes therefore removes the dd^cv term. Also ω∧η_B=0 by dimension, while ∫_P1w=1. Consequently

0≤∫_B(a−δ)η_B.                                       (5)

But a(p)=0 and a is continuous. There is a neighborhood U of p on which a<δ. Choose a nonzero smooth nonnegative top-degree form η_B supported inside U. The right side of (5) is strictly negative, a contradiction. This argument excludes every locally integrable potential defining such a current, hence every genuine global quasi-psh potential in the task. It never restricts a singular current to the exceptional fiber and never changes a canonical value.

For every integer n≥3, choose m=n−1. Equations (3)–(5) produce a nef smooth real background which is not big but has positive fixed-density volume. Thus the unrestricted original conjecture has a negative answer in every such dimension.

All statement-only targets A–D are established by the arguments in n1–n3: global bounded canonical radial admissibility, every projective endpoint, ordinary determinant and normalization, nonclosed nef nonbigness against every genuine potential, the full Gauduchon infimum, every positive-perturbation formula and actual smooth minimizing metric, and the exact original decreasing regularization. No false target or unresolved indispensable mathematical premise was found in this draft. Only the permitted elementary radial calculus, uniform psh limits, distributional Stokes, positivity with smooth forms, matrix AM–GM and ordinary convergence were used.

This conclusion does not settle dimension two or a classification, compute bounded-potential lower Monge–Ampère mass, or assert literature priority. It does not contradict the closed nef Kähler case: X is projective, but dθ≠0. Together, these notes claim a complete solution of the requested negative-answer alternative and every target A–D, subject to their status as unverified proof drafts.

The radial constants are correct. For s=|z|², x=s/(1+s), and q=sF′(s), the Hessian eigenvalues are q/s tangentially and dq/ds radially. Relative to ω they are q/x and dq/dx, so the determinant ratio is (q/x)^(m−1)dq/dx. With the stipulated dd^c normalization, polar integration gives ∫_B b(x)ω^m=m∫_0^1 b(y)y^(m−1)dy. Consequently ∫_B ω^m/a=mt/(m−1)=1. These calculations include the ordinary wedge-power constants.

The smooth approximants are globally valid. Writing qε=x kε^(1/m), the displayed integral defining kε is smooth and positive on a neighborhood of [0,1]. Thus qε is smooth at zero, with dqε/dx(0)=(Hε ε)^(−1/m)>0. At one, qε(1)=1 makes the apparent singularity in φε′ removable. The affine calculation gives Aε^m/ω^m=1/[Hε(a+ε)]. On every infinity chart, x=1−|ζ0|²/S; along ζ0=0 the tangential block remains the Fubini–Study block, mixed terms vanish, and the normal relative eigenvalue is dqε/dx(1)=1/[Hε(1/t+ε)]>0. Together with the origin calculation, this establishes global smooth strict positivity and closedness, rather than merely punctured-chart positivity.

The limiting construction also holds for every m≥2. The two substitutions in J_c establish x≤qε≤x^t directly. Monotone convergence gives Hε↑1, and the normalized flux converges to x^t. The function (x^t−x)/[x(1−x)] is integrable at zero and extends smoothly at one with value 1−t. It dominates the approximating derivatives, giving uniform convergence φε→φ on [0,1]. Adding each chart’s explicit smooth Fubini–Study potential produces continuous uniform limits of psh functions. Therefore φ is genuinely ω-psh everywhere, including its canonical value φ(p)=0. Distributional convergence gives the global positive closed current A. Off p its determinant is t/x=1/a; at infinity its relative eigenvalues are 1 tangentially and t normally. No punctured extension theorem or singular top product is required.

For the full variational lower bound, θ+ηh is strictly positive with potential zero, and dθ=da∧w is nonzero. The pulled-back bounded canonical potential gives Ω=A+aw≥0, smooth strictly positive outside E={p}×P1, where ordinary wedge algebra gives Ω^n=nμ. For every smooth positive Gauduchon γ, distributional Stokes gives ∫θ∧γ^m=∫Ω∧γ^m. The latter is the mass of a nonnegative finite measure. Matrix AM–GM on X\E gives the lower bound n^(1/n)Dμ(γ). E has zero smooth volume, and any current-wedge mass there is nonnegative. Hence λμ(θ)≥n^(1/n) against every admissible metric; no restricted family replaces the infimum. The closed metric h ensures that this family is nonempty and the infimum finite.

The attaining perturbation metrics and every normalization check correctly. More generally, for c,ε>0 put b=a+ε, Ωε,c=cAε+bw, and K=nc^m/Hε. Then Ωε,c^n=Kμ, and γε,c=b^(−1/m)Ωε,c is globally smooth and positive. Its m-th power is b^(−1)c^mAε^m+mc^(m−1)Aε^(m−1)∧w. The first summand is a base top-degree form and the second is closed, so the metric is balanced and therefore Gauduchon. Its numerator is KHε=nc^m and its denominator is K^(m/n)Hε, giving quotient K^(1/n). Stokes and AM–GM give this same lower bound for every Gauduchon test. Thus Vμ(cω+(a+ε)w)=nc^m/Hε, including target C and actual smooth attaining metrics for every ε>0. The optional polynomial-division expression for Hε is also correct.

Using these metrics for θ≤θε and letting ε decrease to zero proves the matching endpoint upper bound, hence λμ(θ)=n^(1/n) and Vμ(θ)=n. Averaging preserves the current inequality and commutes with differentiation. The horizontal distribution dd^c(q∘π) vanishes upon wedging with ω^m, leaving (a−δ)μ≥0, again impossible near p.
